title: Setting stock to zero does nothing
summary: A proto3 scalar cannot tell 0 from unset, so a 0 never arrives. Mark the field optional, regenerate, and test it with has_.

turns.user: partial update api, sending quantity 0 doesn't change the stock. saw in the logs the client sets 0

assistant.body: TL;DR: this is proto3 working as specified. A scalar without optional has no unset state. 0 is the default, so it is not even written to the wire. The receiver cannot tell 0 from unset, and the != 0 check throws both away. Check whether it was sent with has_quantity() instead.

turns.user: doesn't build, no member named has_quantity

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer left out the change to the proto. In proto3, has_ is generated only for fields marked optional. Mark quantity optional and regenerate.
sed -i '' 's/^  int32 quantity = 2;/  optional int32 quantity = 2;/' proto/shop/stock.proto

Note: protoc 3.15 and later accept proto3 optional without an extra flag. The number and type stay the same, so the wire format is compatible. The sender has to be regenerated too, though. A client on the old generated code drops a 0 when it serializes.

turns.user: regenerated the client too. so how do i NOT send quantity now? we used to put 0 there

assistant.body: From now on 0 is an ordinary value that means out of stock. To leave it out, do not call the setter, and on a reused message call clear_quantity() to make it unset again. What the sender meant is what the receiver sees, which makes the contract robust.
